name: Omar Santos

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I work with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What fills a usual shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the afternoon contact centre team handling disputed electricity bills. I can usually spot where a meter reading was entered twice, and I coach agents through the awkward calls rather than taking the headset from them. I have a two-year college diploma and am among the best on this desk. My long service has brought higher pay than most agents here.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does work support outside the centre?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Nadia works in a dental clinic, and our children are eight and twelve. We have a mortgage and nine months of expenses saved. There are plenty of other centres nearby, though a new rate and rota still need checking. I use approved AI search occasionally after another lead tests it on old bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents a short bill summary is useful if they still open the meter history. A duplicated reading can make a polite answer entirely wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect our shifts and my higher lead wage to hold. Nine months saved lets us handle a repair or a job search, though I would rather keep that money intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will keep supervising bill disputes and checking the meter record before an AI reply goes out. In the first year I will replace the money we used for the roof repair from regular pay before we book a longer holiday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job. The roof is fixed, and the reserve can be rebuilt without rushing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do newer agents miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They sometimes look at the amount without seeing two entries for one reading. I ask them to show me the meter date before we promise a refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why put the holiday later?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia and I like travelling with the children, but the roof bill came out of our reserve. We agreed to restore it first.

I would coach agents to spot a **duplicated reading**.
think: I expect our **afternoon shifts** and my higher lead wage to hold because disputed bills still need checking.
I prefer keeping our **nine-month cushion** intact.
do: Keep supervising **bill disputes** and checking meter records.
Restore **roof-repair savings** from regular pay before a longer holiday.

fieldNote: His strong **bill skill** explains the lead role.

steps.text: Keep supervising disputed electricity bills and checking meter readings before AI replies

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the new answer system should be measured by bills reopened, not only chats closed. If the easy questions go, the agents left need time for real disputes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think our team may lose some paid hours, although my experience and nearby centres give me choices. A smaller week would still change our mortgage plan despite the reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will compare the approved assistant with twenty closed double-reading cases and record any reopened bills. If the new review screen becomes required, I will learn it from our quality lead during paid shifts. If my hours fall in the first year, I will apply only to posted paid lead roles with written full-week wages and hours covering our mortgage; I will stay until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about hours, but able to compare real offers. I will not mistake a familiar title for the same wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask colleagues to act together?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not yet. I would show my own case count to the manager and ask for a written rota, then listen to what other agents find.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia and I would put the new rota beside her clinic shifts and the children’s pickup. A centre across town may pay more hourly but cost too much time and travel.

think: I expect some **paid-hour cuts** despite experience.

do: Test **twenty closed bills** and log reopened cases.
Learn **required AI review** on paid shifts with the quality lead.
Apply after cuts for **posted paid leads** with written mortgage-covering wages/hours; compare travel and family rota; stay until signing an offer.

fieldNote: His manager request is **individual**, not group bargaining.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team full thinking AI by 2028 could decide almost every disputed bill. Robots around 2031 are later; they do not extend the life of a headset.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the afternoon queue could close, including my lead post. Nine months saved is a real bridge, but Nadia’s clinic wage alone will not pay our mortgage indefinitely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will request written staffing dates and put a planned kitchen remodel aside. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I will apply for posted paid facilities reception roles only if a written offer states wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and fits school pickup. I will not give notice on a rumour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed at how quickly a whole queue could go. Savings buy us time, not another job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why facilities reception?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have handled visitors to our building when security was short, but I do not know the full job. I would ask for a paid supervised day before treating it as a route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would complete a required safety course if a posted paid role funded the fee and training time. I would not spend the kitchen money on a qualification without a vacancy.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** threatens disputed-bill calls.
I would say **2031 robots** do not delay headset risk.
think: I expect the **afternoon queue** and my post might close.
Nine months saved cannot replace my **lead wage** indefinitely.
do: Request **written staffing dates** and defer kitchen work.
Apply after job ends for **posted paid reception** with written travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup; request a supervised paid day.
Complete **funded required safety training** on paid time only for a posted paid role.
S2.quote: Savings buy us time, not another job.
fieldNote: His visitor experience is **partial**, not a reception credential.
The **course** requires vacancy, funded fees and paid time.
A new role needs **written mortgage-covering net pay**, hours and pickup.

steps.text: Defer planned kitchen remodel while protecting household reserve

Move after closure only on written offer with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages, hours and school pickup
Request supervised paid reception day before treating the unfamiliar job as a route

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives families a chance to inspect the work before calls change. General AI reaches our bills in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might keep the difficult disputes until 2031 and test a reception shift while the lead wage still arrives. I do not assume the building desk lasts forever once robots spread.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep leading the afternoon team and ask a building nearby for a supervised paid reception day if a place is posted. If it posts a paid role with written wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and school pickup and funds the required safety course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only on a signed offer meeting those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but five years lets me check the actual shift. A shadow day without pay does not tell me whether a job feeds a family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the day show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want to see the early opening, visitor checks and how staff handle an injury. I would also check when the shift ends against Nadia’s clinic rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no paid place appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep the higher lead wage while it lasts and look at other posted centres. I will not buy training for a job that exists only in a conversation.

I would separate **2031 desk risk** from later robots.

I know **robots later** could change reception work too.
do: Keep my **afternoon lead shift** while it pays.

feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect a real shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents a decade is time to check actual paid roles without leaving our current seats. Full AGI reaches bill decisions in 2036 and hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I may still be paying the mortgage, but the children will need less collecting. I want to preserve at least nine months of expenses before any risky job move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my lead shift and put part of each pay back into the reserve until it reaches a full year. I will compare posted facilities and contact-centre roles twice yearly. If my call hours fall in the first year after 2036, I will move only for a signed paid offer with full-week wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel, after Nadia and I check both rotas.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the far date, steady about our present wages. Ten years is useful if we keep testing the numbers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a full year?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We already have nine months and my wage is higher than many local offers. A full year would let me refuse a low-paid title if this team eventually shrinks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the children for a job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for a similar centre nearby. We would keep their school unless a signed offer covered the mortgage after moving costs and the new journey.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A whole afternoon queue could close before a building vacancy is real. Written notice, a posted paid job and funded training on paid time would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who signs off a corrected meter reading when the assistant says the case is closed. A bill still lands in a family kitchen. Somebody needs paid time to own the correction.

headlineQuote: A bill still lands in a family kitchen.
portrait: Omar is a **43-year-old skilled lead** with a two-year diploma and higher pay.
His **nine-month reserve**, mortgage, children and plentiful nearby centres give him search time.
He uses **approved AI occasionally** after others test it and keeps meter records central.
He compares **signed paid offers** against current wages, travel and family rotas.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his afternoon queue before a paid alternative appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted paid work and funded training on paid time would help.
